producer_report.summary: Root cause: a priority stated in a BRIEF.md addendum was never an input to plan ordering, and nothing checked the built order against priorities. Fix: BriefTopic now carries a priority, from a `Priority:` line in an addendum or from wording like 'ranks above all other work' or 'top priority'. plan_entry raises a request that serves such an addendum to at least that priority, unless the user set an `athena priority` record. New Plan::priority_violations in plan.rs names any item planned after one of lower effective priority, and drain prints each as a note. Added two tests and a CHANGELOG entry. fmt, clippy, policy scan and athena-core tests pass.

checks_run.note: 50 tests incl. the new order-check test

criteria_check.criterion: The change description names the root cause (owner priority from addenda is not an input to plan ordering and the order is never checked against it) and the fix sits in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs, not in one job's request.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG entry names the cause. The order check is Plan::priority_violations in plan.rs; the addendum input is BriefTopic.priority in reading.rs, applied in plan_entry for every request.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`: a new test builds a plan where an addendum-stated top priority belongs to a newer, later-rung item and asserts it is in the first wave. The same test fails when the change is reverted.
criteria_check.evidence: reading::tests::an_addendum_priority_puts_the_work_serving_it_in_the_first_plan_wave passes (name contains 'plan'); it asserts the newest Implementation-rung item gets Urgent and leads groups[0]. Without the change its priority stays Normal, so the assert fails. I did not run a revert.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`: a new test asserts the order check reports a plan whose top-priority item is not first, and passes a correctly ordered plan. It covers the general case with several items, not one job's ids.
criteria_check.evidence: plan::tests::the_order_check_flags_a_plan_that_puts_a_lower_priority_item_first passes: five generic items with dependency-raised priority, a good built plan, a bad age-ordered plan, and an equal-priority case.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`: all pass, with the existing plan ordering tests (dependencies first, effective priority) unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran fmt, clippy and the athena-core tests, which pass. Existing plan tests are unedited.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry that states the cause and the new check, for an outside reader.
criteria_check.evidence: New first bullet under Unreleased/Added states the cause and Plan::priority_violations.

open_issues: The drain wiring only prints a note when the order contradicts priority, with no integration test. The check cannot trip on orders built by Plan::build, so it is a guard.
mistakes: My first draft of the new reading test had 'plan' missing from its name, so the `plan` filter skipped it. Renamed.
learnings: BRIEF.md addenda have no Priority line today; the 'Speed first' addendum says it 'ranks above all other work', which the new phrase match turns into high.
Effective priority is monotone along a built order, so the check is a single pass over that order.
I did not run the cli drain integration tests; the full suite is left to Athena.
